title: DINOv2: Learning Robust Visual Features without Supervision
layout_note: A data-curation pipeline, not the training architecture: a pair of stacked cylinders on the left (grey 'Uncurated Data' over orange 'Curated Data') feeds three stage columns separated by dashed vertical rules (Embedding, Deduplication, Retrieval) and ends in a pair of stacked cylinders on the right ('Augmented Curated Data', grey over orange).
grouping: Stages are separated by thin dashed vertical rules with bold stage names along the bottom edge. Data source is encoded by colour band: grey cylinder = uncurated, orange cylinder = curated, and the output cylinder stacks both colours to show the mix.
shapes_depth: Database cylinders drawn as flat 2-D cylinders with elliptical tops (grey and orange fills, thin dark outlines). Every image is a real photo thumbnail with a small vertical strip of white cells attached on its right as its embedding vector. Thick black block arrows enter each stage; removed items carry a large red X; the retrieval query image is wrapped in a thick rounded black frame with a grey fill.
proposed_highlight: Operations are shown by what happens to the same photos: duplicates get red X marks, discarded images are faded to low opacity in the retrieval column, and the curated query image in the retrieval stage is the only item in a heavy rounded frame, with an up arrow to the retrieved neighbours.
lesson: Show a data-filtering pipeline by carrying the same real thumbnails through every stage and marking their fate in place (red X for dropped, faded for not retrieved, a heavy frame for the query) instead of drawing process boxes.
notes: Venue from the first page ('Published in Transactions on Machine Learning Research (01/2024)'). This is the paper's only schematic figure; it draws the LVD-142M data-curation pipeline rather than the self-distillation training method (the paper has no training-architecture figure), so it is tagged as a data pipeline.

arrangement.units: Three stage columns (Embedding, Deduplication, Retrieval) separated by dashed vertical rules, each holding three rows of photo-plus-embedding glyphs; open whitespace on both ends holds the input and output cylinders.
arrangement.inputs_as: two stacked database cylinders (grey uncurated, orange curated) containing real photo thumbnails
arrangement.losses_at: none: a data pipeline with no objective
arrangement.shared: the curated stream is a single long black arrow along the bottom row running through all stages to the retrieval query frame, rather than repeated per stage

taxonomy.task: automatic curation of a pretraining image dataset (embedding, deduplication, retrieval)
taxonomy.note: family 'other': the figure draws a dataset-curation pipeline for self-supervised pretraining (DINOv2), not a network; training 'other': no training is drawn, the stages are embedding similarity, deduplication and nearest-neighbour retrieval

core.what: a curated query image travels along one long line under three pipeline stages and, at the Retrieval stage, pulls its nearest uncurated neighbours up out of the deduplicated pool, landing in an augmented curated store on the right

relations.form: the curated image, framed heavy in the Retrieval column, sends an upward arrow into the uncurated column above it; retrieved images stay opaque while unretrieved ones fade and one gets a red X
three columns split by dashed vertical rules with bold names along the bottom (Embedding, Deduplication, Retrieval), each showing the same image thumbnails with their embedding bars
two lanes: uncurated images in the upper rows (from the grey cylinder) and the curated image on the bottom line (from the orange cylinder), running left to right in parallel
each stage's effect is drawn on the samples: red X over removed near-duplicates in Deduplication, faded thumbnails for images not retrieved

channels.colour: store identity: grey cylinder = uncurated data, orange cylinder = curated data; the output store stacks a grey part over an orange part; red X = removed
channels.shape: cylinder = a data store; thumbnail with a striped bar on its right = an image with its embedding
channels.line: thick black arrows = data flow; one long straight line carries the curated query across all three stages
channels.frame: heavy rounded frame = the query image at retrieval; dashed rules = stage boundaries; opacity = kept vs dropped

quality.strengths: Every stage is drawn as its effect on real samples (crossed-out duplicates, faded non-retrieved images) rather than as a module box; the stores are cylinders in a keyed colour that recombine in the output store, so 'curated + retrieved' is visible as geometry; arrows are short and straight.
quality.weaknesses: The same ratatouille photo repeats about ten times with small crop differences, so tracking which copy is which takes effort; the embedding step shows bars attached to images but never shows a model; one red X in Retrieval (on the car) reuses the deduplication mark for a different reason.

insights.structure: Input cylinders on the left and an output cylinder on the right bracket three stage columns split by dashed vertical rules, with bold stage names lined up along the bottom.
insights.data: Every sample is a real food/car photo with a small strip of cells attached as its embedding, and datasets are flat cylinders whose fill colour (grey vs orange) encodes uncurated vs curated.
insights.emphasis: The effect of each stage is drawn on the samples themselves: red X marks over removed duplicates, faded thumbnails for unretrieved images, and a heavy rounded frame around the curated query.
insights.flow: Left-to-right with thick black block arrows entering each column row, and one long thin arrow along the bottom carrying the curated image through to the query frame, from which a short up arrow points to its retrieved neighbours.
insights.avoid: The same ratatouille photo repeats about ten times with only small crop differences, so tracking which copy is which takes effort; distinct samples would read faster.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
